svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: One public port. Every backend call is gated at the edge, so the services themselves carry no auth code.
The only public ingress. Routes by path prefix, and each backend prefix exposes an explicit allowlist of the routes the frontend actually uses.
Allowlisted requests are first probed with forward_auth against userserve /auth/verify (204 = pass, 401 = reject). Anything off the list is answered 403 and never forwarded —
so /vndb/admin, the write routes and /tasks/* stay reachable only on the loopback ports. The API specs are served the same way, under the frontend basePath.
An imgserve cache hit is served straight off disk by file_server — Flask never runs.
Each Flask app runs under its own Waitress thread pool (WAITRESS_THREADS, default 4; userserve 16). All bind loopback only — the edge is the only way in.
APScheduler runs inside the Waitress process — backups, the VNDB crawl jobs, the access-log flush. Celery workers start with enable_scheduler=False, so a job never fires twice.
Five services have a prefix at the edge. logserve does not, and stays reachable on loopback only.
Services import nothing from one another — no shared package, deliberately. They talk over HTTP through the edge, or not at all.
— separate processes; only vndb and imgserve have one
crawl · refresh · bulk edit · relation graph
also the sibling prefetch: asking for one
The crawl schedules walk the Kana API's own listing — newest-first for new entries, plus a cursored
sweep that backfills historical gaps a page at a time.
Stale entries refresh on demand: a stale read is served immediately and re-fetched behind the request.
Runs as a Windows service — the launcher never spawns it,
it only waits for it to accept connections.
One database per service; no cross-database queries:
vndb — mirrored entities, JSONB relation columns + GIN,
soft deletes, and the logs table
imgserve — one row per mirrored image
logserve reads the vndb database · musicserve has none
One server, one logical DB per concern — so no two
1 vndb Celery broker 2 vndb Celery results
4 imgserve Celery broker 5 imgserve Celery results
images/ — the mirrored image cache. Laid out to
match t.vndb.org exactly, which is what lets Caddy
answer a cache hit without consulting Flask at all.
music/ — audio library, scanned from disk;
musicserve keeps no database of its own.
fetch_state.json — per-type crawl cursor, so a
backfill sweep resumes where the last run stopped.
every service reads and writes its own store
file_server — cache hit, Flask never runs
Solid arrow = request path · Dashed arrow = asynchronous or outbound
Pink = the auth path; userserve answers the edge's probe on every gated request
Amber box = a Celery worker, a process of its own — not the web process
Dashed grey box = not exposed at the edge
Ports shown are the standalone ones; under Docker the services keep them internally.
start-prod.ps1 starts three children: Caddy, Next.js, and backend/launch.py prod.
launch.py declares the children and hands them to procserve.Supervisor, which starts them
in dependency order and shuts them down in reverse: Redis, 2 Celery workers, 6 Waitress-served
Flask apps. procserve is a library, not a service — it has no port and nothing routes to it.
PostgreSQL is a Windows service — checked for readiness, never spawned. The dev stack swaps
Waitress for the Flask dev server and adds Flower per worker.
